gloss: to take home; to bring back

definitions.gloss: to take home; to carry back
definitions.explanation: To bring something back to one's home or original location.
To order food for takeout rather than eating at the restaurant.

examples.japanese: お{土産|みやげ}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る。
{会議|かいぎ}の{資料|しりょう}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}って{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I took the meeting materials home and read them.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わらなくて、{家|いえ}に{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: I couldn't finish the work, so I took it home.

examples.japanese: {旅行先|りょこうさき}から{素敵|すてき}な{思|おも}い{出|で}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: I brought back wonderful memories from my trip.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{出張|しゅっちょう}で{得|え}た{知識|ちしき}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}って、{社内|しゃない}で{共有|きょうゆう}した。
examples.english: I brought back the knowledge gained from the overseas business trip and shared it within the company.

examples.japanese: お{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りでお{願|ねが}いします。
この{店|みせ}は{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りもできますか。
examples.english: Can I also get takeout at this shop?

examples.japanese: お{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りですか、{店内|てんない}でお{召|め}し{上|あ}がりですか。
examples.english: Is that for takeout, or will you be eating here?

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}った{料理|りょうり}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りたいのですが、{容器|ようき}はありますか。
examples.english: I'd like to take the leftover food home — do you have a container?

examples.japanese: この{弁当屋|べんとうや}は{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り{専門|せんもん}で、{店内|てんない}で{食|た}べるスペースはない。
examples.english: This bento shop is takeout-only and has no space to eat inside.

notes:
{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {持|も}つ (to hold) + {帰|かえ}る (to return). It means to take something back with you.

ASPECT (ている):
{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}っている indicates the state of having brought something back.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [thing]を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る — to take [thing] home
- [place]から[thing]を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る — to bring [thing] back from [place]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仕事|しごと}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る (take work home)
- お{土産|みやげ}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る (bring back souvenirs)
- {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り{弁当|べんとう} (takeout bento)

TAKEOUT USAGE:
お{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り (with honorific お) is the standard term for takeout food. テイクアウト is also used but お{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り is more traditional.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}む: to bring in (opposite direction)
- {持|も}って{帰|かえ}る: same meaning, less compound-like
